advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Return the decline decision from _inbound_unlink_one instead of re-calling is_confirmed in the caller's elif to count declines.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:575 `if confirm_store is not None and not confirm_store.is_confirmed(`
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:760 `elif confirm_store is not None and not confirm_store.is_confirmed(`
The guard condition is written twice and any future divergence in _inbound_unlink_one's decline logic would not be reflected in the counter.
advisory.finding: The decline count re-invokes confirm_store.is_confirmed(...) in the caller's elif, duplicating the exact check _inbound_unlink_one already performed. The two callsites must stay in lockstep by hand: if the guard in _inbound_unlink_one ever changes (e.g. additional criteria beyond is_confirmed), the counter will silently miscount. Prefer returning the decline signal from _inbound_unlink_one (tri-state or a small result object) rather than re-deriving it.
scenarios: A later change adds another decline reason inside _inbound_unlink_one; the elif still only counts is_confirmed-based declines, so the pass summary under-reports.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only count a decline when an unconfirmed removal would otherwise have deleted a net-active link, so the summary reflects removals actually withheld.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:575-586 early-returns on not-confirmed BEFORE resolving link_uuid
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:601-613 a confirmed-but-absent link is a no-op, NOT counted as declined
The asymmetry means a confirmed no-op counts as nothing while an unconfirmed no-op counts as a 'decline' even though neither would delete anything.
advisory.finding: An unconfirmed removal is counted as a 'declined' removal even when there is no net-active local link to remove (i.e. it would have been a logged no-op regardless). Because the is_confirmed early-return in _inbound_unlink_one runs before the link_uuid resolution, the caller counts every unconfirmed remove record as a decline, inflating the per-pass 'declined N inbound link removal(s)' summary relative to removals that would actually have deleted something.
scenarios: Differ re-emits a removal for a relation the pair no longer holds AND that was never confirmed: counted as a decline each pass, so the summary reports declines that protected nothing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make AC3 actually reproduce the vendor-type-collision path (exercise the outbound differ / G4 suppression) instead of duplicating AC1's generic no-confirmation decline.
evidence: Docstring: 'AC3. The epic's motivating case, end to end. A local ``blocks`` dep whose outbound ADD is permanently deduped by an inward same-vendor-type remote link is never pushed and never G4-protected'

Test body: `applied = apply_records._inbound_update_apply_links(_remove_payload(b, "blocks"), a, repo)` — same store fixture (single a->b 'blocks' link, no confirmation) as AC1, with no vendor-type collision or outbound differ exercised
peer_confirmations.py:8-12 describes the real defect as depending on direction-agnostic ADD dedup on (vendor_type, target_key), which this test does not set up
advisory.finding: test_vendor_type_collision_scenario_is_protected (AC3) claims to reproduce the epic's motivating vendor-type-collision case 'end to end', but its setup and behavior are identical to AC1 (test_declines_removal_of_a_never_confirmed_link): it merely issues a remove for an unconfirmed 'blocks' link. It never constructs a vendor-type collision, never involves the OTHER-direction remote link, and never drives outbound_links._diff_links / the G4 suppression path the defect docstring describes (peer_confirmations.py:8-12). So the collision-specific regression (outbound ADD permanently deduped, never G4-protected) is not actually covered — only the generic no-confirmation decline is.
scenarios: A future change that fixes the generic decline but reintroduces the collision-specific blind spot (e.g. G4 handling or dedup key) would pass this suite
